newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy bankers see key interest rate cut by end-97.
newsitem.headline: Italy bankers see key interest rate cut by end-97.

text.p: The Bank of Italy is expected to cut its 6.75 percent discount rate to 5.75 percent by the end of 1997, the Italian Banking Association (ABI) said.
ABI said in its latest Financial Outlook that it saw the central bank further reducing its key rate by another half percentage point during the course of 1998.

The report said that in the 1997-1998 period the central bank "is seen continuing to closely monitor the market for signs of pressure especially on prices and the lira's exchange rate, and to nip it in the bud."
It said banks participating in the Financial Outlook forecast a decline across the board in money market, bond and bank rates during the rest of this year and in 1998.

The fall in Italian rates is seen taking place against the trend forecast for those in the United States and Germany, ABI noted. This would lead to a further considerable narrowing of the spread between Italian and German rates, the report added.
